articles.title: De dia ou à noite, Jasper revela atrações em todas as estações do ano  | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre montanhas, lagos e geleiras, o parque nacional oferece esqui, trilhas, vida selvagem e um dos céus mais preservados do Canadá para observar estrelas
articles.summary: Entre montanhas, lagos e geleiras, o parque nacional oferece esqui, trilhas, vida selvagem e um dos céus mais preservados do Canadá para observar estrelas
articles.body:
Jasper combina picos montanhosos, florestas, lagos glaciais e algumas das paisagens mais emblemáticas de Alberta. — Foto: Crédito: Luuk Wijk/Tourism Jasper

Cercado por picos de montanhas, geleiras e extensas florestas de coníferas, o Parque Nacional de Jasper é um dos destinos mais completos do Canadá e um dos grandes símbolos das paisagens naturais da província de Alberta. Localizado no extremo norte das Montanhas Rochosas, o parque ocupa mais de 11 mil km² de área protegida e integra, desde 1984, o Sítio do Patrimônio Mundial da UNESCO Parques das Montanhas Rochosas Canadenses, ao lado de Banff, Yoho e Kootenay.

A pequena cidade de Jasper funciona como base para explorar a região e está a cerca de quatro horas de carro de Edmonton, capital da província, além de ser conectada à cidade de Banff pela Icefields Parkway, uma das estradas panorâmicas mais famosas do mundo. Com atrações que mudam conforme as estações, o destino combina aventura, vida selvagem, geleiras e lagos durante o dia com um dos céus noturnos mais preservados do planeta, oferecendo experiências que vão muito além de uma única temporada.

O que diferencia Jasper de muitos outros parques é justamente essa possibilidade de aproveitar as atrações sob a luz do sol ou das estrelas. De dia, trilhas, esqui, cânions e lagos glaciais; de noite, um dos céus mais escuros e acessíveis da América do Norte.

O inverno em Jasper vai de dezembro a fevereiro, seguido pela primavera, entre março e maio, período em que a neve ainda cobre boa parte das trilhas de altitude, mas o gelo começa a derreter nos vales mais baixos.

Marmot Basin é a principal estação de esqui do Parque Nacional. A cerca de 20 minutos de carro da cidade de Jasper, oferece pistas para diferentes níveis de experiência, de iniciantes a esquiadores avançados, em uma área cercada por paisagens montanhosas. A temporada normalmente se estende de novembro a maio, dependendo das condições de neve, e o local também oferece infraestrutura para snowboard.

Em Marmot Basin é possível praticar atividades na neve em uma área cercada por paisagens montanhosas. — Foto: Crédito: Tourism Jasper

O Maligne Canyon Icewalk é uma caminhada guiada pelo interior do Maligne Canyon, cujas cachoeiras se transformam em formações de gelo durante o inverno.

A observação de vida selvagem também é intensa nesse período, com alces, cervos e lobos avistados nos vales abertos, quando a neve empurra os animais para altitudes mais baixas.

Caminhada pelo interior do cânion revela paredes de gelo, cachoeiras congeladas e formações esculpidas pelas baixas temperaturas. — Foto: Crédito: Tourism Jasper

Jasper é sede da Reserva de Céu Escuro (Dark Sky Preserve), uma das maiores do mundo em extensão (mais de 11 mil km²) e reconhecida como a maior reserva de céu escuro acessível do Canadá. A designação foi concedida pela Royal Astronomical Society of Canada em 2011, em parceria com a Parks Canada, e é resultado de medidas como iluminação pública voltada para baixo e redução de poluição luminosa na vila. Com altitudes elevadas e ar limpo de montanha, os céus da reserva são ideais para observar a Via Láctea e a aurora boreal. Noites de inverno, com ar mais seco e mais horas de escuridão, costumam oferecer as melhores condições para a astrofotografia.

O céu noturno, protegido pela maior reserva de céu escuro acessível do Canadá, oferece condições excepcionais para observar estrelas. — Foto: Crédito: Jeanine Holowatuik/Tourism Jasper

O verão vai de junho a agosto, quando lagos e trilhas de alta montanha ficam totalmente acessíveis, e o outono se estende de setembro a novembro, quando as folhagens mudam de cor e as noites voltam a esfriar.

A navegação pelo Lago Maligne até Spirit Island é considerada o passeio mais emblemático do parque: um cruzeiro guiado de cerca de 90 minutos por 14 km de água glacial até a pequena península de Spirit Island, ponto sagrado para os povos indígenas da região.

O cruzeiro pelo Lago Maligne percorre águas glaciais cercadas por montanhas e leva os visitantes até Spirit Island. — Foto: Crédito: Tourism Jasper

O Jasper SkyTram leva os visitantes até o topo da Whistlers Mountain em um teleférico que sobe cerca de 1.000 metros de desnível, revelando vista panorâmica de mais de seis cadeias de montanhas.

O Jasper SkyTram leva os visitantes até o alto da Whistlers Mountain, de onde se descortina uma vista panorâmica das Montanhas Rochosas, do vale e lagos da região. — Foto: Crédito: Tourism, Jasper

Passeios de caiaque no Lago Maligne e trilhas junto a geleiras, como as que levam à Columbia Icefield e ao glaciar Athabasca, completam a lista de atividades diurnas de verão e outono.

O Maligne Lake impressiona pelas águas de origem glacial, cercadas por picos das Montanhas Rochosas. — Foto: Crédito: Charles Hill/Tourism Jasper

A vila de Jasper reúne dezenas de restaurantes para jantares tranquilos depois de um dia de trilha, muitos deles com vista para as montanhas.

Embora não sejam garantidas, auroras boreais ocasionais podem ser vistas em noites de céu limpo, sobretudo longe das luzes da vila.

O Jasper Planetarium, instalado próximo ao Fairmont Jasper Park Lodge, oferece sessões sob cúpula e observação com telescópio guiada por astrônomos.

O auge da vida noturna do parque acontece em outubro, com o Jasper Dark Sky Festival, festival anual de astronomia com shows, palestras e observação de estrelas.

O Jasper Dark Sky Festival celebra a astronomia com palestras, experiências, música e observação de estrelas. — Foto: Crédito: Tourism Jasper

Jasper pode ser acessado de carro por duas das principais rodovias da região: a Icefields Parkway, para quem vem de Banff, ou a Yellowhead Highway, a partir de Edmonton. Para observar estrelas, as noites próximas à lua nova são as mais indicadas, e a programação ganha destaque em outubro, durante o Jasper Dark Sky Festival. Já o passeio de barco até Spirit Island, no Lago Maligne, ocorre normalmente do fim de maio ao início do outono.

A recomendação da Parks Canada é consultar o mapa interativo What’s Open antes de montar o roteiro, para conferir quais atrações, estradas, trilhas e serviços estão disponíveis durante a visita. As informações estão disponíveis no link What's open in Jasper National Park - Jasper National Park .

articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSTU ao governo de Santa Catarina teve compromissos de campanha em Florianópolis nesta segunda-feira (14).
articles.summary: Candidato do PSTU ao governo de Santa Catarina teve compromissos de campanha em Florianópolis nesta segunda-feira (14).
articles.body:
Professor Marcus Sodré concede entrevista à NSC TV nesta segunda-feira — Foto: NSC TV/Reprodução

O candidato ao governo de Santa Catarina Professor Marcus Sodré ( PSTU ) cumpriu agenda de campanha nesta segunda-feira (14) em Florianópolis e Balneário Camboriú.

Durante a manhã, realizou panfletagem no bairro Itacorubi, em frente à Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina (Udesc), em Florianópolis. No começo da tarde, gravou entrevista na NSC TV.

À tarde, seguiu viagem para Balneário Camboriu, onde à noite tem reunião com o comitê de campanha para realizar o alinhamento dos compromissos da semana.

Em entrevista para a NSC TV, respondeu de que forma pretende ampliar as parcerias público-privadas em Santa Catarina.

"O nosso candidato a presidente pelo PSTU, Hertz Dias, tem defendido nacionalmente o fim das terceirizações. Nós entendemos que as parcerias público-privadas são uma forma de transferir verbas do Estado para as empresas privadas. Nós vamos acabar com isso contratando novos servidores e investindo mais dinheiro nos serviços públicos".

🔍 A campanha eleitoral de 2026 iniciou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Desde esta data, candidatos estão autorizados a pedir votos e realizar comícios, caminhadas, debates e divulgar suas propostas em rádio, TV e internet, seguindo as regras estabelecidas pela Justiça Eleitoral.

articles.title: What could stop the Houthis’ advance across Yemen?
articles.summary: Iran-backed group seized areas on Red Sea coastline.
articles.body:
Already war-torn and under blockade for more than a decade, Yemen risks descending into another civil war.

The Houthis have tightened their grip on islands in the Red Sea, giving them control over a vital global shipping route.

The fighting has unravelled a shaky ceasefire that had largely held since 2022. It comes as the Iran war has disrupted maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

So, what does it mean for this volatile region?

articles.title: Paes promete ampliar Transolímpica da Avenida Brasil até Nova Iguaçu | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PSD também propôs estender a Via Light até a Avenida Brasil e Cabuçu e transformar área do antigo aeroporto em parque público.
articles.summary: Candidato do PSD também propôs estender a Via Light até a Avenida Brasil e Cabuçu e transformar área do antigo aeroporto em parque público.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio de Janeiro pelo PSD, Eduardo Paes , prometeu ampliar a Transolímpica a partir da Avenida Brasil até o Centro de Nova Iguaçu , na Baixada Fluminense, passando por Nilópolis e Mesquita, com a implantação de um sistema de BRT em todo o trajeto.

A proposta foi apresentada durante uma atividade de campanha em Nova Iguaçu. Segundo Paes, a extensão da via expressa teria como objetivo reduzir o tempo gasto pelos moradores da Baixada nos deslocamentos e conectar a região à rede de transporte da capital.

"Primeiro, fazer com que a TransOlímpica, que eu fiz como prefeito do Rio, saia da onde ela chega na Avenida Brasil, passe por Nilópolis e Mesquita, e chegue no centro de Nova Iguaçu com BRT, conectando toda a rede BRT da cidade do Rio de Janeiro.", comentou Paes.

Paes afirmou que a proposta busca enfrentar o tempo elevado de deslocamento enfrentado por moradores da Baixada Fluminense.

"Das cinco cidades do Brasil com maior tempo de mobilidade das pessoas, quatro estão na Baixada Fluminense", completou.

Paes promete ampliar Transolímpica da Avenida Brasil até Nova Iguaçu — Foto: Reprodução TV Globo

Paes esteve em Nova Iguaçu no início da manhã e apresentou, além dos projetos de mobilidade, propostas para ampliar as opções de lazer na cidade.

Outra proposta de mobilidade apresentada por Paes é ampliar a Via Light para conectá-la à Avenida Brasil e, no outro sentido, estendê-la até Cabuçu, em Nova Iguaçu.

Segundo o candidato, o corredor também seria atendido por BRT e funcionaria como alternativa à Estrada de Madureira.

"Uma outra proposta é fazer com que a Via Light chegue a Avenida Brasil, também conectando com o BRT da TransBrasil e vá até Cabuçu, que é uma alternativa, também toda ela com BRT", explicou o candidato.

Paes afirmou que as duas intervenções poderiam melhorar a circulação de veículos e oferecer alternativas para quem utiliza o transporte público.

Eduardo Paes em Nova Iguaçu — Foto: Reprodução TV Globo

Além das propostas de mobilidade, Paes afirmou que pretende transformar a área do antigo aeroporto de Nova Iguaçu em um parque público.

A ideia é criar o Aero Parque de Nova Iguaçu, com áreas de lazer, cultura e convivência. O candidato citou como referência parques implantados durante sua gestão como prefeito do Rio.

"Vamos fazer disso aqui um grande equipamento de lazer de Cultura, a exemplo do Parque Madureira, do Parque Realengo, do Parque Oeste, que nós fizemos na cidade do Rio de Janeiro, trazendo alternativa de lazer, de contemplação de qualidade para o povo da Baixada.", disse Paes.

Segundo Paes, a área também poderia receber estruturas para ajudar no combate às enchentes.

O candidato afirmou que pretende aproveitar parte da área para criar estruturas de acumulação de água da chuva e reduzir o risco de alagamentos.

Paes também citou a possibilidade de instalar equipamentos culturais e de lazer no espaço.

articles.title: Sebrae abre processo seletivo com salários de até R$ 7,7 mil no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições iniciaram nesta segunda-feira (14) e seguem até o dia 30 pelo site da Fundação de Apoio à Pesquisa, Ensino, Tecnologia e Cultura (Fapetec). Há vagas para analista técnico I e assistente II.
articles.summary: Inscrições iniciaram nesta segunda-feira (14) e seguem até o dia 30 pelo site da Fundação de Apoio à Pesquisa, Ensino, Tecnologia e Cultura (Fapetec).
articles.body:
Processo seletivo vai contratar profissionais para trabalhar no Sebrae Acre — Foto: Ascom Sebrae no Acre

O Serviço de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas no Acre (Sebrae Acre) abriu inscrições nesta segunda-feira (14) de um processo seletivo para contratação de profissionais e formar cadastro de reserva para os cargos de analista técnico I e assistente II.

As inscrições seguem até 30 de setembro pela internet, no site da Fundação de Apoio à Pesquisa, Ensino, Tecnologia e Cultura (Fapetec) , responsável pela organização da seleção.

Os salários variam entre R$ 4.801,10 e R$ 7.783,25, de acordo com o cargo. Os profissionais contratados também terão direito aos benefícios oferecidos pelo Sebrae-AC, como auxílio-alimentação, vale-transporte, assistência médico-hospitalar, plano de previdência privada, seguro de vida em grupo, auxílio educação, auxílio atividade física e auxílio especial.

Segundo o edital, o processo seletivo terá três etapas e todas vão ocorrer de forma remota. São elas:

Avaliação de conhecimentos (prova objetiva e discursiva)

Os candidatos aprovados serão contratados pelo regime da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT). O contrato será por tempo indeterminado, com jornada de 40 horas por semana.

A seleção oferece vagas para profissionais com ensino médio e superior. As oportunidades são para diferentes áreas de formação, entre elas administração, jornalismo, direito, ciências contábeis e sistemas de informação, além de outras graduações.

articles.title: Brasileira desaparecida em Veneza: taxista é investigado por morte | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com jornais italianos, suspeita é de que condutor navegou acima do limite de velocidade no Canal de Tessera. Buscas por Gabriela Elorriaga chegaram ao terceiro dia na Itália.
articles.summary: Buscas pela brasileira desaparecida em Veneza entram no 3º dia enquanto piloto de táxi aquático é investigado por homicídio náutico e excesso de velocidade.
articles.body:
Equipes fazem busca por brasileira que desapareceu em Veneza após acidente náutico. — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O piloto do táxi aquático envolvido na colisão que causou a morte do pescador italiano Sean Michieli, de 25 anos e o desaparecimento da brasileira Gabriela Querino Elorriaga , de 26, é investigado por homicídio náutico pelas autoridades da Itália.

Segundo informações divulgadas pela agência de notícias italiana ANSA e pelo jornal Corriere della Sera , o condutor foi ouvido formalmente pelos investigadores.

As apurações iniciais apontam que a embarcação de transporte de passageiros trafegava em velocidade superior ao limite permitido para o Canal de Tessera no momento do impacto.

O g1 entrou em contato com o Ministério Público da Itália para obter detalhes sobre o andamento das investigações, mas não obteve resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Na legislação italiana, o homicídio náutico é equiparado a um homicídio causado por acidente de trânsito em vias terrestres e prevê pena de 2 a 7 anos de prisão para quem é condenado.

"A legislação italiana, a princípio, é bem semelhante à brasileira, tem a mesma origem, no direito romano, só que nesse caso específico ela acaba sendo mais rigorosa do que a nossa (...). Aqui no Brasil nós não temos um homicídio náutico, seria um homicídio culposo, com uma pena bem menor, de um a três anos", analisa o advogado Daniel Pacheco.

O acidente aconteceu na madrugada de sábado (12), por volta das 5h (horário local), no Canal de Tessera, importante via náutica da Lagoa de Veneza que dá acesso ao Aeroporto Marco Polo.

O barco de pesca ocupado pelo casal afundou imediatamente após ser atingido pelo táxi aquático.

O marido da brasileira, Sean Michieli, chegou a ser resgatado com traumatismo craniano grave e levado a um hospital em Mestre, onde teve a morte cerebral confirmada no domingo (13). Gabriela caiu na água no momento da colisão e não foi mais vista.

Equipes fazem buscas por Gabriela Elorriaga, que desapareceu em Veneza após acidente náutico. — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Nesta segunda-feira (14), os trabalhos de resgate entraram no terceiro dia consecutivo sem que a brasileira fosse localizada.

O Corpo de Bombeiros e a Polícia de Veneza mobilizam equipes de mergulhadores, embarcações equipadas com sonar para varredura do fundo do canal e sobrevoos com helicóptero.

As operações enfrentam forte complexidade por conta das características da própria região do Canal de Tessera, marcada pela água turva, baixa visibilidade subaquática e intenso tráfego de embarcações.

Gabriela Elorriaga e o marido, Sean Micheli, se envolveram em um acidente na madrugada de sábado (12), em Veneza — Foto: Redes sociais

Natural de Ribeirão Preto (SP), Gabriela morava na Itália há dois anos e havia se casado com Sean em junho deste ano, em uma cerimônia realizada em Veneza.

O casal residia na Ilha de Burano. Sean pertencia a uma família com tradição de gerações dedicadas à pesca local, e Gabriela estava providenciando a documentação e a habilitação náutica para trabalhar formalmente na pesca ao lado do marido.

De acordo com familiares, navegar por aquela área fazia parte da rotina diária dos dois.

No Brasil, a mãe da jovem, Gisele Elorriaga, declarou que ainda mantinha a esperança de encontrar a filha com vida. A família viajou à Itália para acompanhar os trabalhos de resgate no local.

O italiano Sean Michieli, de 25 anos, e a brasileira Gabriela Querino Elorriaga, de 26, em Veneza, na Itália. — Foto: Redes sociais

articles.title: Homens são condenados por matar jovem sem antecedentes e que iria se mudar para Portugal | G1
articles.standfirst: Crime ocorreu em julho de 2025, no bairro Bela Vista, em Curvelo. Jurados reconheceram motivo fútil e recurso que dificultou a defesa da vítima.
articles.summary: Crime ocorreu em julho de 2025, no bairro Bela Vista, em Curvelo. Jurados reconheceram motivo fútil e recurso que dificultou a defesa da vítima.
articles.body:
Local onde o crime ocorreu — Foto: Redes sociais

Três homens, de 23, 24 e 24 anos, foram condenados a 27 anos de prisão pelo homicídio de um jovem, 19 anos, ocorrido em julho de 2025, no bairro Bela Vista , em Curvelo .

"A vítima havia concluído o ensino médio, não tinha antecedentes criminais e tinha planos de ir morar em Portugal com o tio no mês seguinte ao crime", informou o Ministério Público de Minas Gerais (MPMG) nesta segunda-feira (14).

Segundo o MPMG, o crime ocorreu quando os três condenados passavam de carro por uma avenida da cidade e avistaram a vítima, que estava acompanhada de dois amigos adolescentes, cada um em uma bicicleta.

Ainda de acordo com a denúncia, teve início uma discussão entre os envolvidos, com troca de xingamentos. Em seguida, os ocupantes do veículo retornaram em direção ao jovem e continuaram a acompanhá-lo em baixa velocidade.

"A discussão continuou e os réus, ainda dentro do veículo, passaram a seguir a vítima em baixa velocidade. Um deles, de 24 anos, sacou uma arma e efetuou disparos contra o jovem. Conforme o laudo pericial, os tiros causaram a morte da vítima ainda no local.

Após o crime, segundo o Ministério Público, os réus teriam debochado da vítima, rido da situação e fugido. Na sequência, roubaram a motocicleta de um vigia da cidade e a esconderam na fazenda de um familiar de um deles.

"Na sequência eles esconderam o carro utilizado no homicídio na casa de um amigo e se esconderam, por cerca de três dias, na residência de um deles. O revólver utilizado no crime foi vendido com o objetivo de se desfazer da arma. Dois dos réus foram condenados pelo roubo da moto e um deles foi absolvido."

O Ministério Público informou que recorreu da decisão para tentar reverter a absolvição e obter o reconhecimento da participação dele no assalto.

Um dos condenados já havia sido responsabilizado por um triplo latrocínio contra dois idosos e uma pessoa com deficiência física. Conforme o MPMG, as vítimas foram amarradas e mortas com tiros na nuca, e o autor roubou dinheiro delas. Por esse caso, ele foi condenado a 31 anos de prisão.

Sobre o julgamento realizado em Curvelo, o Ministério Público destacou que "os jurados reconheceram as qualificadoras apontadas pelo MPMG: crime cometido por motivo fútil e com uso de recurso que dificultou a defesa da vítima".

O MPMG também informou que os réus devem cumprir as penas em regime inicial fechado. O processo tramita em segredo de Justiça.

articles.standfirst: A chuva de granizo atingiu o distrito de Nova Cardoso, em Itajobi (SP), na tarde desta segunda-feira (14).
articles.summary: Moradores registraram uma chuva de granizo que atingiu o distrito de Nova Cardoso, em Itajobi (SP), na tarde desta segunda-feira (14).
articles.body:
Moradores registraram uma chuva de granizo que atingiu o distrito de Nova Cardoso, em Itajobi (SP), na tarde desta segunda-feira (14).

O vídeo enviado à reportagem da TV TEM mostra o momento em que a grande quantidade de pedras caiu sobre casas, automóveis e ruas do distrito. Assista acima.

Chuva de granizo em Itajobi (SP) — Foto: Reprodução / WhatsApp

O g1 questionou a Defesa Civil sobre possíveis estragos e prejuízos, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Na região de São José do Rio Preto (SP), a população recebeu o alerta sobre o mau tempo enviado por meio de celular pela Defesa Civil.

Com a chuva, as temperaturas baixaram. A mínima para esta segunda-feira é de 17 graus.

Segundo o OpenMeteo, a probabilidade de chuva para esta terça-feira (15) é de 75%. Na quarta (16) e quinta-feira (17), o sol deverá aparecer na região de São José do Rio Preto. Todavia, para sexta-feira (18) e sábado (19), a previsão é que a chuva volte. Nesta semana, a mínima é de 15 graus e a máxima poderá chegar a 33 graus.

articles.standfirst: Segundo a SSP, veículo estava estacionado em frente à casa do proprietário quando se movimentou sozinho neste domingo (13); dono caiu ao tentar sair da residência e precisou de atendimento médico.
articles.summary: Segundo a SSP, veículo estava estacionado em frente à casa do proprietário quando se movimentou sozinho; dono caiu ao tentar sair da residência e precisou de atendimento médico.
articles.body:
Caminhão desgovernado atinge carro, derruba poste e para dentro de córrego em Indaiatuba (SP) neste domingo (13) — Foto: Marcos MT Estética Automotiva

Um caminhão desgovernado atingiu um carro e um poste de iluminação pública, invadiu uma área de mata e foi parar dentro de um córrego no Jardim Morada do Sol, em Indaiatuba (SP), na tarde deste domingo (13).

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, o caminhão estava estacionado em frente à residência do proprietário, quando se deslocou de forma desgovernada.

Na trajetória, o veículo colidiu com um Renault Kwid e destruiu um poste de iluminação pública.

Segundo a Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSP), o dono do caminhão, de 51 anos, caiu ao tentar sair de casa e foi encaminhado à UPA para atendimento médico.

O caso foi registrado como dano no Plantão da Delegacia de Indaiatuba.

articles.title: EUA anunciam primeira arma espacial em órbita | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretário da Força Aérea do país, Troy Meink, disse que equipamento será usado para proteger tropas americanas de adversários. Dispositivo teria a capacidade de destruir satélites inimigos, segundo autoridade ouvida pelo 'Washington Post'.
articles.summary: Secretário da Força Aérea disse que equipamento será usado para proteger forças americanas
articles.body:
Vista aérea do Pentágono, nos EUA, de 3 de junho de 2011 — Foto: Charles Dharapak/Arquivo/AP Photo

O secretário da Força Aérea dos Estados Unidos , Troy Meink, afirmou nesta segunda-feira (14) que o país já posicionou armas espaciais em órbita. Ele não informou quais são os equipamentos nem deu detalhes sobre seu funcionamento, segundo o "Washington Post".

“Os Estados Unidos agora têm, em órbita, armas de controle espacial capazes de defender as forças conjuntas contra adversários hostis”, disse Meink durante discurso na conferência Air, Space, Cyber, realizada em National Harbor, no estado de Maryland, perto da capital do país.

É a primeira vez que os EUA reconhecem publicamente possuir uma capacidade ofensiva no espaço. Durante anos, Washington acusou a China e a Rússia de realizar manobras militares em órbita, incluindo o uso de lasers e técnicas de interferência para ameaçar satélites americanos.

Um funcionário do governo ouvido pelo jornal "The Washington Post" sob condição de anonimato disse que o dispositivo teria a capacidade de destruir um satélite inimigo, caso ele esteja sendo usado para alvejar tropas ou satélites americanos.

Autoridades de alto escalão das Forças Armadas americanas costumam ser cautelosas quando questionadas sobre as armas espaciais dos EUA e frequentemente citam questões de segurança nacional.

A declaração também representa uma mudança significativa no discurso oficial. Em 2022, John Raymond, primeiro chefe de operações espaciais da Força Espacial dos EUA, afirmou que “nosso principal objetivo é impedir a guerra”.

Meink não forneceu detalhes adicionais sobre o tipo de armas em órbita que os Estados Unidos possuem.

Ele também afirmou que os interceptadores baseados no espaço, tecnologia central do sistema de defesa antimísseis Golden Dome, do presidente Donald Trump , estão agora “prontos para o voo”.

articles.title: Quem era o professor que morreu após passar mal em academia no Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Jeyres Pereira Nobre, de 55 anos, chegou a receber massagem cardíaca de outras pessoas que estavam no local, mas não resistiu. Amigos o descreveram como alegre e simpático.
articles.summary: Jeyres Pereira Nobre, de 55 anos, chegou a receber massagem cardíaca de outras pessoas que estavam no local, mas não resistiu. Amigos o descreveram como alegre e simpático
articles.body:
Jeyres Pereira Nobre era professor de optometria em Fortaleza (CE) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O homem de 55 anos que morreu após passar mal enquanto se exercitava em uma academia em Fortaleza , nesta segunda-feira (14), foi identificado como Jeyres Pereira Nobre, professor de optometria e dono de uma ótica no bairro Autran Nunes. A causa da morte não foi divulgada.

Jeyres administrava a NR Óptica, há 12 anos, junto com a esposa. Ele era professor do curso técnico em Ótica do Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem Comercial do Ceará (Senac), no bairro Centro, desde 2003, e do curso de Óptica e Optometria da Faculdade Cruzeiro do Sul, ambos na capital cearense.

Amigos e colegas de profissão descreveram Jeyres como alegre e simpático. "Ele era fantástico, brincalhão. Você não via ele mal em momento nenhum. Recebia todo mundo" , relembra o vice-presidente do Conselho Regional de Óptica e Optometria do Ceará (Crooce), José Bezerra.

Conforme apuração do g1 , o optometrista estava na academia Smartfit do bairro Dom Lustosa, no início da manhã, quando teve um mal súbito. Ele chegou a receber massagem cardíaca por outras pessoas que estavam no local e também teria recebido estimulação elétrica pelo desfibrilador. O Samu também foi acionado, mas Jeyres não resistiu e morreu dentro do estabelecimento.

Conforme a Secretaria da Segurança Pública e Defesa Social do Ceará (SSPDS), equipes da Polícia Militar foram acionadas para a ocorrência e, somente após o laudo da Perícia Forense, será possível confirmar a causa da morte do homem . O caso está a cargo da 21ª Delegacia de Polícia Civil da capital.

Em nota, a academia Smart Fit lamentou a morte do aluno e informou que a vítima recebeu os primeiros socorros no local. "A equipe prestou imediatamente os primeiros socorros e acionou o Samu, que também realizou o atendimento no local. Infelizmente, o óbito foi constatado. Lamentamos profundamente o ocorrido e nos solidarizamos com os familiares e amigos", disse a Smart Fit.

Essa é a segunda morte registrada em uma academia de Fortaleza entre agosto e setembro. Em 12 de agosto deste ano, uma adolescente de 17 anos faleceu após passar mal em uma academia no Bairro João XXIII. À época, testemunhas relataram nas redes sociais que a jovem estava caminhando na esteira quando desmaiou. Ele chegou a ser levada a um hospital, mas morreu.

Por meio de nota, o Conselho Regional de Óptica e Optometria lamentou a morte de Jeyres. "A CROOCE recebe com profunda tristeza a notícia do falecimento do Professor Jeyres, cuja trajetória e dedicação deixaram marcas importantes naqueles que tiveram a oportunidade de aprender e conviver com ele", disse a entidade.

A faculdade Cruzeiro do Sul também lamentou a morte do docente e suspendeu as aulas do curso .

"Hoje nos despedimos de um grande professor, amigo e um exemplo de dedicação. O professor Jeyres deixa um legado de conhecimento, humanidade e muitos ensinamentos que ficarão para sempre em nossos corações", disse a faculdade.

Personal e alunos fizeram os primeiros socorros

Ao g1 , o personal trainer Geislan Sampaio, que estava na academia, relatou ter participado dos primeiros socorros ao professor Jeyres Nobre. Ele disse que, por volta de 6h10, uma aluna o informou que uma pessoa estava passando mal na área de musculação.

"Foi quando corri, ele já estava no chão ao lado da máquina e vários alunos em volta dele", relembra o Geislan, que possui curso na área de primeiros socorros. Ele, uma aluna que é enfermeira e outro aluno tomaram a frente e iniciaram os procedimentos de massagem cardíaca. Ele relata que encontrou o professor já com os sinais vitais fracos.

Homem morre após passar enquanto se exercitava em academia de Fortaleza. — Foto: Reprodução

Conforme o profissional, após o início da massagem cardíaca, uma funcionária da academia foi pegar o desfibrilador do estabelecimento. A aluna que é enfermeira realizou os procedimentos com a máquina, mas ainda assim o pulso do professor não retornou.

Ainda conforme Geislan Sampaio, o Samu foi acionado tão logo Jeyres foi encontrado ao chão, mas a equipe só chegou cerca de 30 minutos depois. Eles realizaram procedimentos de reanimação, porém o óbito foi confirmado no local.

O personal conta que costumava ver o professor na academia pela manhã cedo e que, comumente, ele o cumprimentava. "Sempre muito educado e alegre", lembra.

Em abril, as academias de Fortaleza receberam recomendação para reforçar o cumprimento de normas que garantam a segurança dos consumidores. A orientação foi repassada pelo Programa Estadual de Proteção e Defesa do Consumidor (Decon), um dia após a morte de um aluno que se exercitava em uma academia do bairro Parreão .

Na recomendação, o Decon orientou que as academias exijam atestado médico no ato da matrícula , realizem avaliação prévia dos alunos, garantam o acompanhamento por profissionais habilitados e adotem protocolos de emergência.

A recomendação do Decon, que integra o Ministério Público do Ceará (MPCE), também vale para as empresas intermediadoras de acesso a esses serviços, como as plataformas Gympass, TotalPass e similares.

O g1 procurou o Decon para entender se as recomendações já estavam em vigor e, caso sim, se estava havendo fiscalização. A reportagem será atualizada quando houver resposta.

Entre julho de 2025 e agosto de 2026, em Fortaleza e na Região Metropolitana foram registradas 7 mortes em academias. Relembre os outros casos:

➡️13 de julho de 2025 : o policial civil Francisco José Alves da Silva Júnior, de 47 anos, morreu enquanto realizava um treino em uma academia de Fortaleza . Ao g1, amigos informaram que ele sofreu um infarto.

➡️13 de outubro de 2025 : um homem identificado como Cristiano Silva Honorato, de 44 anos, morreu após sofrer um mal súbito em uma academia da rede Gaviões, também em Fortaleza. A causa da morte não foi informada.

➡️20 de outubro de 2025 : um homem identificado como Artur do Nascimento, de 45 anos, morreu da mesma forma , em outra unidade da rede Gaviões. A causa da morte também não foi informada.

➡️25 de outubro de 2025 : a empresária Áurea Maria Rodrigues, de 45 anos, morreu durante uma aula de spinning em uma academia da rede Greenlife, em Maranguape, na Região Metropolitana de Fortaleza. Segundo a família, ela teve um Acidente Vascular Cerebral (AVC).

➡️17 de dezembro de 2025 : uma aluna morreu em uma academia da rede SmartFit localizada na avenida Engenheiro Santana Júnior, no bairro Papicu. Ela recebeu os primeiros atendimentos médicos, mas não resistiu e morreu no local.

➡️22 de abril de 2026 : o professor de Educação Física Renan Guedes morreu em uma academia da rede MaxForma, no bairro Parreão, em Fortaleza. A causa da morte não foi informada.

articles.title: Attacks on church services worry community, clergy
articles.summary: BCP condemns mob attack on a house church service in Dantan, West Midnapore; woman abducted and rescued, police probe urged, peace rally set for Sept 21.
articles.body: Kolkata: Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP), a forum representing Christian communities in Bengal and parts of east and northeast India, has expressed deep anguish over repeated attacks on the community in the state. In the latest incident, a house church service in Dantan, West Midnapore, was attacked on Sunday by a mob of 40-45 chanting ‘Jai Shri Ram’. A female devotee was abducted and later rescued by police.On Sunday, the mob allegedly issued a directive demanding an immediate halt to all church services.Ashalata Murmu, who was leading the Sunday morning service, remains traumatised. Recounting the ordeal to TOI, she said, “We hold morning prayers every Sunday at Ram Nayak’s house. I reached the spot around 9 am and began the service. At 9.30 am, we noticed a crowd outside the house, calling Nayak out. Hearing an argument, we stepped outside. Some of them ordered us to stop services immediately, citing govt orders.”She added, “One of them confronted us, saying, ‘‘Tumi jano na sarkar bolechhe Girja Masjid bondho. Esob ar kora jabe na (Don’t you know the govt has declared that churches and mosques are closed? None of this can be done anymore).”When Nayak expressed ignorance of any such directive and refused to comply, he was physically assaulted.As female worshippers attempted to resist the aggression, they, too, were assaulted. Among them, Chumki Singh was allegedly dragged by her hair, abducted, and held captive by the miscreants for at least two hours. Officers from Dantan Police Station, alerted by locals, rescued Singh. An official from Dantan Police Station said no formal complaint has been registered yet.BCP founder state secretary Herod Mullick said, “We have seen frequent attacks over the last few months. We appeal to the govt to take stringent action, identify the culprits, and initiate punitive measures against them.”BCP Dantan Zone Committee has announced a ‘Peace and Prayer Rally’ on Sept 21, starting at God’s Church and proceeding towards Dantan Police Station to spread a message of peace and harmony.(With inputs from Sujoy Khara)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: North Wales Police officer who punched suspect 9 times in head faces misconduct hearing
articles.summary: PC Richard Williams faces eight allegations relating to an arrest in a police misconduct hearing.
articles.body:
A police officer who punched a suspect nine times in the head used unreasonable force on multiple occasions, a police misconduct hearing has been told.

PC Richard Williams faces eight allegations relating to the arrest of Steven Clark, including using a headlock or "choker", unreasonable use of incapacitant spray, and throwing or dropping Clark into the back of a police van.

A misconduct hearing at North Wales Police headquarters in Colwyn Bay heard Williams denies wrongdoing.

He was cleared of assault and intentional strangulation following a seven-day trial in Caernarfon, Gwynedd, in 2025.

In May 2023, police were called to Porthmadog in Gwynedd, following a report of a domestic argument.

A woman told officers, Clark, then 34, was "off his head on wacky backy" and possibly other drugs.

The misconduct hearing was played several clips of police body-worn camera footage, as well as mobile phone video recorded by onlookers.

When police tried to arrest Clark, the misconduct hearing was told things "take a turn", and the suspect ended up on the ground.

It is alleged Williams used handcuffs to "cause pain to Clark's wrist", who "winced and reacted".

It is also alleged he put Clark in a headlock, which it is claimed was "unreasonable".

Clark claimed he "could not breathe", and later suggested during police interview he was losing consciousness.

It is also claimed Clark "is punched by Williams nine times in the face or head", and that "punching Clark nine times in the face was not a reasonable use of force".

The hearing was told "it is nine pretty quick punches" with no pause for reflection.

Four allegations relate to the use, or apparent use, of incapacitant spray.

Another is that Clark was "thrown or dropped into the van" while trying to resist.

It is claimed the eight allegations "amount to an unreasonable use of force".

The hearing was adjourned until Tuesday.

articles.title: Sudan aid networks at risk of collapse, UN agencies warn
articles.summary: Without immediate donations, shelter and aid relief supplies could be depleted by the end of the month, says IOM.
articles.body:
Sudan’s aid network is at risk of collapse, the United Nations’ International Organization for Migration (IOM) has warned.

Ongoing fighting , heavy rains, and continued displacement threaten to bring an “imminent end” to Sudan’s emergency relief supply via the IOM’s Common Humanitarian Pipeline, the agency said on Monday.

The ongoing war between the Sudanese army and the rival paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that erupted in April 2023 has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and created the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis. But amid a sharp cutback in global aid funding, resources are stretched.

“The entire humanitarian system could collapse within weeks if we don’t act now. Without new funding, we won’t be able to get help where it’s needed most,” said Amy Pope, IOM’s director general in a statement.

“We simply can’t turn our back on the people of Sudan when they need us most amid raging conflict, increased displacement and the impact of heavy rain,” she added.

The IOM warned that without immediate donor support, shelter and aid relief supplies are expected to be depleted by the end of the month. The operational capacity of warehouses that keep the pipeline functioning is only able to be sustained until the end of the year.

A total of 8.6 million people remain internally displaced in Sudan, with ongoing violence, floods and heavy rains continuing to damage shelters and forcing people to move, the organisation said.

IOM said its network, comprising nearly 100 national and international NGOs, has supplied aid to 2.8 million people since July 2023. However, its reach has been shrinking due to falling funds, even as needs remain at an all-time high.

The cost of keeping the IOM system running for a year to support 305,000 people is $15m, and the agency would require $42m to return to the level of aid it was able to provide in 2024.

Funding for Sudan at the World Food Programme (WFP) has also fallen, dropping by about half this year, its acting head told the Reuters news agency.

Executive Director Carl Skau said that while access had represented humanitarians’ largest obstacle in the past, now “we have [a] presence that we are not fully utilising because of the lack of funding”.

Last year, WFP received $645m in funds, but so far this year funding is only at $206m.

Meanwhile, in continued fighting, at least four civilians were killed and several others wounded overnight in RSF drone attacks on Damazin, the capital of Blue Nile region, a senior Sudanese military official told Al Jazeera.

The official said the attacks targeted civilian infrastructure and fuel stations owned by civilians.

articles.title: Perez Hilton enters residential treatment program following self-harm incident
articles.summary: Five weeks after he engaged in self-harm during a livestream, celebrity blogger and podcaster Perez Hilton has entered a residential treatment program, his family said in an update.
articles.body: Five weeks after he engaged in self-harm during a livestream, celebrity blogger and podcaster Perez Hilton has entered a residential treatment program, his family said in an update. “This was an important next step, but there’s still a long road ahead,” Hilton’s family wrote in a statement. The Miami-based internet personality is expected to remain in the program for at least several more weeks. He does not have access to his phone or laptop, and contact with family and friends remains limited, according to the update. “Perez is alive, he’s getting help, and he’s surrounded by people who want to see him healthy and happy again,” the family said. The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Department responded to his home on Aug. 4 after reports emerged that the single father of three was livestreaming self-harm. The video, which was streamed on TikTok before the platform pulled it, appeared to show Hilton covered in blood, with visible cuts and holding what appeared to be a knife. Viewers pleaded with him and asked for his phone number so they could alert authorities. Hilton, 48, became famous in the early 2000s for publicizing and sometimes belittling celebrities who made public gaffes or found themselves in legal trouble. His brand of Hollywood gossip mixed with occasionally mean-spirited commentary made him an instant online sensation but also contributed to his reputation as a toxic, if amusing, personality. In 2010, he apologized for participating in bullying behavior. He recently moved with his three kids to Miami from their home in Las Vegas. His three children are safe and remain in the care of their grandmother, the family said in Monday’s update. “We are incredibly grateful for the continued outpouring of love, kindness, and well wishes for Perez and his children. Every thoughtful message has been appreciated,” the statement read. Since the Aug. 4 incident, rumors have swirled online that Hilton lost his memory and is covered in gauze from injuries sustained during his mental health crisis. His family dispelled those rumors on Monday and asked the public to stop spreading malicious gossip about Hilton. “Perez has spent years acknowledging, apologizing for, and genuinely trying to grow from the things he said and did earlier in his career,” his family said in their statement. “The internet has a way of preserving old versions of people, even when the person behind them has changed. No one has to forget his past or accept his apologies. But we hope we can all agree that celebrating someone’s suicide attempt crosses a line.” If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7, to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

articles.title: Texas landowners sue Trump administration over border, Big Bend construction
articles.summary: The “Conserve Big Bend” coalition says the administration is using its power to build a wall in among the most remote and ecologically significant land with very little border crossings.
articles.body: A group of private landowners in western and southwestern Texas filed a federal lawsuit Monday to stop the Trump administration from building border walls, barriers and roads through their properties. The group includes some property owners and local residents who were up in arms a couple of years ago demanding better enforcement along the border and criticizing the Biden administration for spikes in immigrant border crossings. The lawsuit was filed by Conserve Big Bend, an umbrella group that includes a coalition of about 230 landowners, and six plaintiffs. It was filed in Washington, D.C. The plaintiffs allege the administration has wrongly designated the area along the Texas border as one of “high illegal entry.” The Trump administration did so, the lawsuit states, to invoke “extraordinary power” to build a border wall on their property in “one of the most remote, rugged and ecologically significant stretches of the United States.” But in 2025 the Customs and Border Protection’s Big Bend sector, which stretches over 77 counties and the state of Oklahoma, tallied the fewest number of apprehensions — just 1.3% — among the total of nine southwest border sectors, according to the lawsuit. The same has been true in the last five years, when the Big Bend sector accounted for 1.16% of apprehensions and had the lowest number each year, according to the lawsuit. Holding signs that read “Landowners against Border Wall,” landowners and their supporters stood Monday at the Presidio County Courthouse in Marfa, where the filing of the lawsuit was announced at a news conference. Some wore their summer cowboy hats and large silver belt buckles, while others held aloft flags of Texas and the U.S. One flag flown said, “Don’t Mess with Big Bend.” “We spoke real loud when our border was being invaded. And as a two-time Trump voter, you know the border’s secure. Thank you, thank you, President Trump. You’ve secured the border, but now let it go,” Laura Allen, a Val Verde County rancher and a former Val Verde County judge, said at the news conference. Allen, who’s not named in the lawsuit but is part of Conserve Big Bend, told those gathered of how she was repeatedly on Fox News and other media outlets when “we had the Haitian crisis in Del Rio.” In 2021, more than 10,000 immigrants, mostly from Haiti, were packed by Customs and Border Protection under an overpass bridge in Del Rio, a city in Val Verde County, as border officers scrambled to keep up with a surge in crossings. But now immigration enforcement-related construction threatens land that has been in Allen’s husband’s family since 1920, she said. The project will go through the middle of their property, Allen said, which lies close to Lake Amistad and the Rio Grande boundaries. According to her, the construction plans would put “working facilities” behind “walls,” which would cut off a subdivision of about 100 retirement homes and weekend getaways built on their property. NBC News reached out Monday to the Department of Homeland Security, which did not have immediate comment on the lawsuit. The administration paused construction and survey work in Big Bend National Park last month. Rodney Scott, who heads Customs and Border Protection, said on X at the time that CBP was pausing “all construction activity in Big Bend National Park while I visit and conduct a personal, on-the-ground evaluation.” The arrival of heavy equipment and the clearing of desert flora were shared on social media, sparking backlash. That pause is due to expire Sept. 30. But landowners with property outside the park say their property is at risk. According to Conserve Big Bend, 65% of the 609 miles of the planned Big Bend sector border project is on private property. According to the lawsuit, coalition members who own property in Hudspeth, Brewster, Presidio and Val Verde counties have received written notices from CBP identifying their land as potentially needed for the border wall project. David Keller, a regional archaeologist and Conserve Big Bend board member, owns a 10-acre farm in Presidio County. He uses his property for boating, guiding river trips and for his own enjoyment, the lawsuit states. He fears the project will cut his access to the Rio Grande, affect irrigation and make his land unusable for farming, the lawsuit stated. He said Conserve Big Bend formed as landowners began to receive letters from the government. Organizers rushed to identify landowners, contact them, hold landowner meetings, educate them and urge them not to sign away their rights. “We brought this challenge because for us Big Bend is not an empty place on a map. It is our home,” Keller said. Joaquin Peña said at the news conference his family has farmed land in Redford, Texas, for many generations “and now there is an imminent threat coming to our way of life.” “Farming is the backbone to our community, and now we’re being told that we have to give up land for a threat that doesn’t even exist,” Peña said. “Yet the real threat is the government taking away land from honest Texans, and that’s just not right.” William Zuberbueler owns about 1,800 acres and more from family and cousins. The Val Verde County land has been in his family since the 1880s and, over the years, the government has taken parts of it for various projects, he said. In the 1980s, the government “required us to relinquish our land” for construction of U.S. Highway 90, Zuberbueler said. In the 1970s, some of the land was needed to protect rock art in Seminole Canyon State Park, he said, and before that, in the 1960s, the family lost portions of the land during the years Lake Amistad was built. Between February and July of this year, CBP sent Zuberbueler multiple notices regarding 11 specific tracts where it may need to enter for construction-related work on his land, according to the lawsuit. “Our land, which my brother still actively ranches, running sheep, goats and cattle, our birthright, is now being taken by an administration that has promised to protect it,” he said.

articles.title: Texas bought a 1,700-acre Hill Country ranch for a new state park; unlike nearby Garner, planners want it rugged, with Frio River access only after miles of backcountry hiking
articles.summary: US News: Texas park authorities have acquired a 1,720-acre ranch in Uvalde County to create Bear Creek State Park, offering outdoor visitors a more natural and.
articles.body: Texas park authorities have acquired a 1,720-acre ranch in Uvalde County to create Bear Creek State Park, offering outdoor visitors a more natural and rugged alternative to the heavily developed recreation areas nearby. According to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD), the property was purchased for $33.5 million using a one-time state appropriation. It sits less than a mile from Garner State Park, the most visited park in the state system. However, officials plan to develop Bear Creek in a very different way. Unlike Garner, where visitors can park close to the river and use paved areas, reaching the spring-fed Frio River at Bear Creek will require visitors to travel for miles through steep canyons, limestone ridges, and backcountry trails.A deliberate shift toward backcountry conservationAccording to TPWD, limiting vehicle access near the river is part of an effort to expand public recreation while protecting the environment. Garner State Park often reaches capacity by noon on summer weekends, with large numbers of visitors using its developed lawns, roads, and river access areas. Bear Creek, by comparison, is planned around quieter and lower-impact outdoor activities. Initial surveys found dense forests, steep ravines, and oak grasslands across the property. According to state officials, these areas contain sensitive habitats and support the endangered golden-cheeked warbler as well as several rare plant species found in the deeper canyons.Texas Governor Greg Abbott also highlighted the recreational value of the purchase when announcing the acquisition. “The acquisition of Bear Creek State Park will provide Texans access to the Frio River along with streams, canyons, and hiking trails for visitors to explore,” Abbott said. “I encourage all Texans and out-of-state visitors to witness our beautiful Texas parks up close.”Immersive trails instead of paved parking lotsAccording to preliminary plans from TPWD, Bear Creek State Park will focus on exploring the landscape rather than driving directly to recreation areas. Park planners are developing a network of natural-surface trails through the Balcones Canyonlands. The trails are expected to connect visitors with scenic viewpoints overlooking Old Baldy, the well-known landmark within nearby Garner State Park. Visitors heading toward the Frio River and its tributaries, including Spring Creek and Bear Creek, will use backcountry trails designed to reduce damage to sensitive areas along the waterways.According to early public-use plans, the park will also offer walk-in campsites, primitive backpacking areas, and dark-sky viewing locations. These options will take priority over large recreational vehicle areas and paved parking lots. David Yoskowitz, executive director of TPWD, said the new park would give people another way to experience the Texas Hill Country. “The department is excited to add Bear Creek to the Texas State Park system and provide Texans with another picturesque slice of the Texas Hill Country to enjoy,” Yoskowitz said. “The rolling grasslands and unnamed creeks stretching across the landscape will one day provide visitors with a new place to explore the peaks and valleys that make up Uvalde County.”Funding the next generation of public landsAccording to TPWD, development of Bear Creek will be supported by the $1 billion Centennial Parks Conservation Fund. Texas voters approved the dedicated fund in 2023 to help speed up land purchases and park development across the state. Under agency policy, newly acquired state park property must provide some form of public access within 18 months of purchase, while full park operations are expected within four years. According to preliminary plans, limited public access, including guided hikes and special events, is expected to begin in late 2026 while natural and cultural resource surveys are completed.Paul Foster, chairman of the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission, said the purchase reflects the state’s wider effort to create more public outdoor spaces as Texas continues to grow. “This latest land purchase is another feather in the cap of the department for their efforts to provide more public spaces for Texans to recreate in the outdoors,” Foster said. “Combined with the previous additions, Texas has added more than 6,800 acres of new parkland.”Preserving cultural heritage and dark skiesThe Bear Creek property also has an important human history. According to early archaeological surveys, researchers have found evidence of Native American campsites on the land, including old cooking areas and places where tools were made along the creek beds. The property later became part of the region’s ranching history. Historical records indicate that in the late 1800s, rancher Abraham B. “Abe” Kelly established a homestead where Bear Creek and Spring Creek meet. According to park planning information, officials also want to protect the area’s natural night sky. By limiting artificial light and avoiding large amounts of overnight infrastructure, planners hope to preserve the darkness of the Hill Country while highlighting the property’s cultural history. As public meetings and feedback sessions continue, officials are working on the park’s final master plan. According to TPWD, Bear Creek State Park is expected to become a destination for hikers, birdwatchers, and backpackers looking for a quieter and more natural experience of the Frio River valley.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Mahmoud Khalil lawsuit says Columbia failed to protect pro-Palestinian activists
articles.summary: Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil sued Columbia University on Monday, alleging it failed to address harassment against him and other members of a pro-Palestinian campus group and retaliated against them when they reported it.
articles.body: Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil sued Columbia University on Monday, alleging it failed to address harassment against him and other members of a pro-Palestinian campus group and retaliated against them when they reported it. The university’s “deliberate indifference” led to the doxing of multiple group members and Khalil’s detention by immigration agents, according to the civil rights lawsuit filed in federal court in New York City. At a news conference announcing the lawsuit, Khalil accused the university of “discrimination aimed at intimidating Palestinian students.” “We are suing because no student, regardless of their background, should go through the hell that Columbia put us through over all these years,” he said. The university declined to comment on the lawsuit, but said in an email that “creating a campus environment where every member of our community feels welcome, supported, and safe is fundamental to who we are as a University.” “Columbia is committed to protecting our community from discrimination and harassment, and responding promptly and appropriately when concerns arise,” it said. Khalil also sued Columbia last year to block the release of student records to a congressional committee. A former graduate student at Columbia University, Khalil gained prominence as a spokesperson for student activists protesting Israel’s actions in Gaza. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents arrested him at his apartment on campus in March 2025, and he quickly became the face of the Trump administration’s crackdown on pro-Palestinian demonstrators. Khalil spent 104 days in a Louisiana immigration jail, missing the birth of his first child, before a federal judge in New Jersey ordered his release. His deportation case remains active. Khalil’s latest lawsuit says Columbia “refused to correct disinformation” while he was detained, “allowing a false narrative about his conduct and role to persist and further enabling peer-on-peer harassment of other Palestinian students and students with perceived shared Arab and/or Muslim ancestry.” Instead of investigating reports of harassment, the university retaliated by characterizing events by a pro-Palestinian campus group as security risks and revising disciplinary policy to target criticism of the Israeli government, according to the lawsuit. At the news conference Monday, Khalil also accused the university of surveilling pro-Palestinian students and hiring private investigators to monitor him. The lawsuit accuses Columbia of civil rights violations, requests a court order restoring Khalil’s access to the campus and ending the Palestinian group’s suspension, and seeks damages “to be determined at trial.” It also names the pro-Palestinian group and its president, Mohammad Zubairi, as plaintiffs.

articles.title: Finland shelters under French nuclear umbrella amid Russian, US uncertainty
articles.summary: Finland becomes 10th European state to sign up to military cooperation and nuclear deterrence initiative.
articles.body:
Finland has agreed to join France’s Forward Deterrence Initiative, extending the coverage of the French nuclear deterrent to eleven European countries.

The announcement came as part of a new strategic partnership between Finland and France, formalised by the countries’ foreign ministers in Helsinki on Monday. Finland becomes the 10th European country to join the French initiative, which comes as Russia is viewed as a growing threat and increasing concern over the commitment of the United States to help protect the continent.

“Finland has decided to join forward deterrence,” according to their joint statement.

Finnish President Alexander ‌‌Stubb wrote on social media that the initiative is “first and foremost about strengthening European security”.

A nuclear steering group will be set up in the coming months to begin implementing the cooperation, the two European Union states announced.

Stubb was careful to state that the initiative does not replace NATO’s nuclear deterrence, insisting that the move had been discussed extensively with the US ⁠⁠and the military alliance.

However, Finland joins Britain, Germany, Poland, Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, Greece, Denmark and Norway in signing up for cooperation with France’s nuclear umbrella, as President Donald Trump’s shake-up of NATO has Europe – and especially those states closer to Russia in the east – reassessing their security arrangements.

Estonia is also in discussion with France with an eye on joining the enhanced nuclear deterrence, Prime Minister Kristen Michal told the AFP news agency.

“We are under NATO’s nuclear umbrella already. And France is also backing up our independence with the troops in Estonia. So if the cooperation can be deeper in the nuclear field, that probably will go so,” he said.

Under the initiative, the French president ⁠⁠alone has the authority to decide when nuclear weapons are used, in contrast to NATO, which has a shared Nuclear Planning Group.

However, it offers joint ⁠⁠exercises, the potential short-term deployment of nuclear-capable assets on allied territory and deeper consultation.

Finland does not intend to allow nuclear weapons to be ‌‌stationed ‌‌on its territory in peacetime, Stubb noted.

Finland is among a number of European countries that warn of the growing threat from Russia.

Finnish authorities seized a vessel in December suspected of intentionally severing undersea telecommunications cables amid fears of Russian sabotage in the Gulf of Finland.

The Fitburg was en route from the Russian port of St Petersburg ⁠⁠to Israel at the time of the incident, according to Finnish officials.

articles.title: Multiple vehicle road crash in South Africa kills 21
articles.summary: Fatal traffic accidents are a recurring problem for South Africa.
articles.body:
A road accident involving multiple vehicles on one of South Africa’s main routes has killed 21 people.

The collision on the N1 highway in the early hours of Monday involved two Toyota minibus taxis and a Suzuki sport utility vehicle, police spokesperson Warrant Officer Christopher Spies told reporters.

The collision in Western Cape, South Africa’s southernmost province, was one of two major crashes in the country over the past two days. Eight people were killed in an accident near Ermelo in Mpumalanga province early on Sunday. Fatal traffic accidents are a recurring problem for South Africa.

Monday’s accident closed the N1 highway 380km (240 miles) east of Cape Town, between the small towns of Prince Albert and Leeu-Gamka, the Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC) said.

The death toll “may change as emergency services and authorities in the Western Cape continue their assessment of the scene”, according to the road safety agency.

Eighteen people were declared dead at the scene of the crash, while three others were announced dead after being taken to a hospital, bringing the toll to 21, said Spies. Another four people were seriously injured.

Nearly 11,500 people died in road accidents in 2025, according to the country’s Transport Ministry.

In 2023, a head-on collision between a tour bus and a cash-in-transit truck left 20 people dead and at least 60 others injured in the northern Limpopo province.

articles.title: In 2011, a Massachusetts dairy installed the state's first agricultural digester; by 2020, manure and food waste were saving it $155,000 a year on heat, fertiliser, and bedding
articles.summary: US News: For generations, cow manure was simply an unavoidable byproduct of running a dairy farm. At Jordan Dairy Farms in Rutland, Massachusetts, however, it .
articles.body: For generations, cow manure was simply an unavoidable byproduct of running a dairy farm. At Jordan Dairy Farms in Rutland, Massachusetts, however, it became something much more valuable: a source of electricity, heat, fertiliser and even animal bedding. In 2011, the family-run dairy installed what it describes as the first agricultural anaerobic digester in Massachusetts. The system uses microorganisms to break down manure and other organic waste in an oxygen-free environment, producing biogas that can be used to generate electricity.Randy Jordan, who runs the farm with his brother Brian, was looking for a way to deal with rising electricity costs. Jordan Dairy Farms had hundreds of cows producing manure every day, and Jordan began exploring whether that waste could be converted into energy. The answer was anaerobic digestion.By 2020, the system was saving the farm roughly $155,000 a year through heat, fertiliser, and bedding produced from what would otherwise have been waste.How does a manure digester work?The science behind the system is based on a natural biological process. Organic material such as manure contains compounds that microorganisms can consume. Inside an anaerobic digester, the material is kept without oxygen, allowing microbes to break it down and release a mixture of gases, including methane and carbon dioxide. The methane can then be burned to generate electricity and heat.At Jordan Dairy Farms, manure is not the only material entering the digester. Food and beverage waste collected from businesses is mixed with the farm's manure, increasing the amount of organic material available for digestion.According to Vanguard Renewables, which operates the system, the farm's digester receives around 20,000 tons of food waste and 9,125 tons of manure every year. The material is processed inside a 500,000-gallon digestion tank.Microorganisms break down the mixture, producing biogas that powers two engines. Together, the engines have a capacity of about 800 kilowatts and generate approximately 4,200 megawatt-hours of renewable electricity annually, according to Vanguard.Manure becomes electricity, heat and fertiliserThe process produces several useful outputs, turning one waste stream into multiple resources for the farm. The electricity generated by the system can be used on the farm, while excess power has also been sold directly to nearby businesses. The heat generated during the process is another important benefit. In 2020, Jordan told The Washington Post that heat and hot water produced by the digester saved the farm around $35,000 a year.The farm also receives a huge volume of liquid fertiliser from the digestion process. Jordan said at the time that the system produced about 14 million gallons of liquid fertiliser annually, saving the farm roughly $100,000 in fertiliser costs. The solid material left behind could also be used as animal bedding, providing another estimated $20,000 in annual savings. Together, those savings amounted to around $155,000 a year.The current project information from Vanguard similarly lists reduced energy costs, low-carbon fertiliser, heat reuse, reduced chemical fertiliser use and odour reduction among the farm's benefits.Why add food waste to cow manure?The idea of putting food waste into a manure digester was particularly important to the project's economics. When Jordan first investigated digesters, the technology had already existed for decades. But many earlier systems struggled financially and operationally. According to The Washington Post, energy consultant Bill Jorgenson proposed combining food waste with manure. The additional organic material could increase energy production, while companies looking to dispose of food waste could pay fees to have that material processed.That created a second revenue stream around the same piece of infrastructure. The arrangement also addressed another environmental problem: organic waste sent to landfills can generate methane as it decomposes. Capturing organic material in a controlled digester instead allows much of that methane to be collected and used.For the farm, waste from food processors and other businesses becomes an input rather than something with no value.What happens to the methane?The biogas produced by the digester contains methane, which is the component used to generate energy. At Jordan Dairy Farms, the gas is directed to generators that produce electricity. The heat produced in the process can also be recovered and used around the farm. The farm's own website says the digester generates enough clean energy each day to offset approximately 5,500 pounds of carbon dioxide emissions, while Vanguard estimates annual renewable electricity production at 4,200 MWh.The system has since expanded beyond the original installation. Jordan Dairy Farms says a second digester was added at its Spencer, Massachusetts, facility in 2016. The Rutland operation itself has also become part of a larger network of farm-based renewable-energy projects.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jethmalani: Why wasn't FIR slapped on Varma?
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Leading lawyers Harish Salve and Mahesh Jethmalani Monday advocated a reset in the judiciary, as happened after the Emergency, and said the.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leading lawyers Harish Salve and Mahesh Jethmalani Monday advocated a reset in the judiciary, as happened after the Emergency, and said the complaint redressal mechanism needs to be reformed for the public to continue reposing faith in the institution.Referring to the unprecedented discovery of burning cash at Justice Yashwant Varma's residence in March last year, Jethmalani asked why an FIR was not registered given that the judge had repeatedly moved the SC seeking the quashing of the inquiry.Jethmalani said there is a dire need for the infusion of transparency in the working of the judiciary. Salve asked if a minister would have escaped an FIR if such an incident had happened at their residence. What would have been the judiciary's response to a PIL on such an incident being reported from the residence of a person who was not part of the judiciary.CJI Surya Kant, responding to the queries at the Ram Jethmalani Memorial Lecture, said the internal mechanism to deal with complaints against judges is robust, responsive, and expeditious."No doubt every system and mechanism can be improved. But I can assure you that the internal mechanism to deal with complaints against judges has been adequate," he said.CJI Kant said most of the complaints against judges are filed by disgruntled litigants after suffering a reversal in court."Would it be proper to adjudicate these complaints in the public domain? If so done, what happens to the judges and the judiciary?" the chief justice asked.Salve said the courts must stick to their field: the law."When they deviate from that, the results have been devastating. Court-monitored investigations are a myth. What happened in the 2G spectrum allocation scam, coal block allocation scam, and Hawala scam cases, investigations into which were monitored by courts? When the court monitors an investigation, the investigating agency loses its independence and feels obliged to deliver results, and that is when things get skewed," Salve said.He said a strong judiciary is welcome. "When it is strong at a time when govt is weak, everyone applauds it for raising questions. But when there is a strong govt, the public judges the judiciary on how often it raises questions before the govt. It is then that the balance between the three organs gets disturbed," he said.Jethmalani criticised the opaqueness in the appointments and transfers of judges in constitutional courts and said the area needs reforms to allay apprehensions of favouritism and nepotism.CJI Kant said the collegium system has evolved over the years, and the smooth manner in which the appointments and transfers take place in consultations with govt shows that there is little reason to doubt its efficacy.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: A stunning stretch of Cornish coastline has gone on the market for £3 million, prompting concern among locals who fear the much-loved beach could be snapped up by a wealthy developer or celebrity.Loe Beach, near Feock, has been enjoyed by local residents and visitors for generations. However, villagers in the affluent area, which has been dubbed ‘millionaire’s row’, are now worried about what the future could hold for the popular stretch of coastline.The more than six-acre site includes around 78 metres of foreshore, a private beach, car park, boat storage, café, watersports facilities and grazing land.Parish council calls public meeting over Loe Beach saleConcerns over the future of the site have been significant enough for Feock Parish Council to arrange a public meeting later this month.According to SWNS, the council said it had been contacted by several worried residents and acknowledged the strength of feeling surrounding the sale.“Loe Beach is a much-loved and valuable community facility and we understand the strength of feeling about its future,” the parish council said.Members of the public will be able to attend and speak during the public participation session at the council's next meeting on Monday, September 21, at 6pm at the Old Market Hall, Market Street, Devoran.Locals fear millionaire buyer or developer could take over beachResidents in the area, dubbed ‘millionaire’s row’, have expressed concern that the £3 million asking price could attract a wealthy buyer, celebrity or developer.One local resident questioned how many people in Cornwall could afford the property and warned of a possible influx similar to what has happened in parts of Devon.“I wonder how many people in Cornwall can afford that? I see an invasion coming on like a few places in Devon,” the resident said.Another added, “They do call it millionaire’s row. I just hope it’s not bought by a developer.”Others said they hoped the strong feeling among local residents about maintaining access to the beach would ensure it remained accessible to the community.“There’s enough rich folk there who want access to ensure it doesn’t get made totally private,” one resident said.Another objected to the idea of privately owning the coastline, saying, “No part of our coastline should ever be private with the exception of MOD requirements. It is outrageous how they can sell off the shoreline in Cornwall.”What is included in the £3 million sale?The property, located on the western shore of the Fal Estuary, is renowned for its tranquil setting. The sale includes more than six acres of land and 78 metres of foreshore.The landholding includes a private beach, a beachside car park that also doubles as boat storage, a cafe, watersports facilities and grazing land.The current owners receive income from the car park and rents paid by commercial operators based at the site.Property agents call it a ‘special piece of real estate’Property consultants Vickery Holman, who are handling the sale, described Loe Beach as a “special piece of real estate” and said there had already been strong interest from prospective buyers.A spokesperson said the site offered immediate access to the Fal River, making it a haven for watersports enthusiasts.The property has remained in family ownership for many generations and is now being offered for sale by informal tender.The agents said a new owner could either maintain the existing arrangements or consider sensitively improving the facilities, subject to obtaining the necessary permissions.“Ample opportunity exists for a new owner to either maintain the status quo or to sensitively improve facilities. Either way this is a special piece of real estate,” the spokesperson said.For residents of the affluent ‘millionaire’s row’, however, the main concern remains whether Loe Beach will continue to be accessible to the community after its new owner takes over.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
